To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EVA_GA descriptor is an improvement on EVA, that EVA is a good alternative to CoMFA, and that the EVA descriptor is a valuable tool for QSAR studies.
the use of a genetic search to find optimal values for the smearing parameters in the EVA descriptor leads to improved QSAR models.

the use of the GA approach for searching the optimal smearing function (EVA_GAs) for a series of 5 different data sets (including 2 data sets with a test set of compounds not used in training) resulted in models with better predictive properties than the original EVA approach and that the use of a grid resolution of 2 Å for the CoMFA approach resulted in models with predictive properties comparable to those of the EVA and EVA_GA models.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a robust method of molecular representation for QSAR studies, which is capable of being applied to a wide range of biological targets and which is insensitive to the precise details of the 3D structure.
the use of a genetic algoritm in the search for models with optimal predictive properties and the effect of grid spacing upon CoMFA models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EVA descriptor is a very powerful tool in the QSAR toolbox.

the EVA_GA technique, in combination with the use of a genetic search algorithm to optimise the standard deviation of Gaussians used to smear frequencies in different spectral regions, has been shown to be a powerful tool for generating predictive models for the QSAR of diverse sets of compounds.
EVA_GA models are more stable and more predictive than either EVA or CoMFA models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EVA descriptor, when optimised by a genetic algorithm, is a useful alternative to CoMFA in QSAR studies.
the EVA descriptor is a robust and effective tool for QSAR studies and that the EVA_GA technique is a powerful method for searching for optimal descriptor values.
EVA_GA models, with their enhanced predictive properties, are more robust than CoMFA models, which are more sensitive to grid resolution, and that EVA_GAs are superior to standard EVA models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of localised σ values can improve the performance of the EVA method.

the EVA_GA technique can produce models with predictive properties comparable to those of CoMFA, but with the additional advantage that the models are insensitive to the alignment of the compounds in the training set.

the use of a genetic search for the optimal localised values for σ can improve the predictive performance of the EVA method and that this is particularly the case when a small number of compounds is available for training.
